title: Read commands and the planning group still diverge from the QCLI-264 payload shape
description:
Follow-up from QCLI-264, which the orchestrator deliberately scoped to the task lifecycle and draft mutating commands. Two divergences were found during that work, verified against source, and left alone rather than silently widened:

1. milestone create / decision create return {record, result} instead of the bare record. QCLI-103 made them return a record at all; it never unified the shape. opum-cli-e2e suites/45-parity-backlog.mjs:293,298,448 read .record?.id today, so changing it is a second breaking change with its own consumer list.

2. draft view returns the located record {draft, location} while task view returns the task bare. This is the read group, not the mutating group, so it is a different contract question: whether location belongs in the payload at all, or beside it.

Neither is urgent. The value of deciding is that 'where is the record in data' should have one answer a caller can rely on without checking per command.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision exists for whether the planning group (milestone/decision create) adopts the bare-record shape or keeps {record, result}, with its consumer list enumerated first as QCLI-264 did
A decision exists for whether read commands carry the located wrapper (draft view) or the bare record (task view), applied consistently across the read group
Whatever is decided is pinned by a test alongside the QCLI-264 shape test

plan: 1. Measure the current shapes rather than assume them: planning mutations return {record, result:{kind,revision}}; draft view/list return {draft, location}; every other read (task view/list, milestone view/list, decision view/list) is already bare.
2. Enumerate consumers by BARE FIELD NAME (record, result, draft, location) across the fleet, state the grep pattern in the record, and read every hit rather than trusting the shape of the match.

3. Planning mutations (milestone/decision created/updated/archived/deleted) return the bare record. result is the same mutation wrapper QCLI-264 removed elsewhere -- same unwrap, same conflict-classification fix.

4. draft view/list flatten to the draft fields plus location inline, mirroring task view/list which carry path inline. Keep the name location rather than renaming to path: it is the field drafts already expose and what --include-archived consumers filter on, and renaming would be a second gratuitous break.
5. Extend test/qcli264-mutation-payload-shape.test.ts (or a sibling) to pin the planning and read shapes alongside the ones QCLI-264 fixed, so all of it moves together.
6. Land on dev behind bun run check, in the SAME stacked pair as QCLI-264 -- one breaking envelope change per release, not two across two.
implementationNotes:
Consumer enumeration (orchestrator condition 1), done before any code change, by BARE FIELD NAME as instructed.

Pattern matched, stated so the next reader can see the shape of my blind spot: for each of record / result / draft / location, the regex [."'[]<field>\b -- the field name preceded by a dot, a quote, or a bracket, with no assumption about the access idiom around it. That is deliberately noisier than QCLI-264's grep, which matched data?.id ?? data?.task?.id and missed 45-parity-backlog.mjs:250 because its fallback was written in the reverse order. Counts across opum-cli-e2e's suites/lib/bin/test, lore-cli/src, opum-fleet hooks and skills: record 45, result 98, draft 48, location 3. Every hit read, not just the ones whose shape looked like an envelope access.

BREAKS (1, in a repo I do not own): opum-cli-e2e suites/45-parity-backlog.mjs:298 asserts typeof questData(questDecision)?.record?.id === 'string' on decision create, with no fallback -- that check fails after the unwrap. Line 293 reads the same path to build the row's 'actual' string, which is cosmetic (it would render 'id=undefined') but sits in the same row. Reported to that session.

SURVIVES, already tolerant: 45-parity-backlog.mjs:448 reads created?.record?.id ?? created?.id on milestone create.

SURVIVES, shape-agnostic: every draft view/list consumer in opum-cli-e2e (21-quest-records.mjs:273, 285-304) tests with JSON.stringify(data(...)).includes('<id or title>'), so flattening {draft, location} to the draft's own fields plus location keeps them passing. 10-contract-quest.mjs:24 asserts only the envelope kind.

UNAFFECTED: lore-cli never calls a planning or draft command -- REQUIRED_COMMANDS at src/adapters/quest.ts:106-119 is manifest, version, init, the migration group, task status-flow/list/view/search/create/edit. Its only three 'location' hits (src/commands/check.ts:988,1135,1137) are HTTP redirect headers, not our field. opum-fleet's hooks read task list --json, task view --plain and task edit --add-note only.

INTERNAL: quest-cli's own src/cli/main.ts:549 (nextDraftId) reads record.draft.id off the SERVICE type, not the envelope, and is untouched -- listDrafts still returns LocatedDraft; only the CLI's presentation flattens.

Version call (orchestrator condition 3): ships in the SAME stacked pair as QCLI-264, not a later one. One breaking envelope change per release rather than two across two, so a consumer adapts once. Both are on dev unreleased under the same Unreleased changelog section; no version field, tag or publish in either change.

Consequence I had to fix while writing this: the QCLI-264 changelog paragraph ended with 'milestone create and decision create keep {record, result}; unifying the planning group is not part of this change (QCLI-265)'. True when written this morning, false the moment 265 joined the same release. Removed rather than left to ship as a stale claim in the release notes -- a sentence that was accurate when written and is false now is exactly the decay opum-fleet named today (a measured snapshot is a fact about a moment, not a standing fact), and an unreleased changelog is the easiest place in the repo to leave one.
finalSummary:
Both divergences QCLI-264 deliberately left are closed, in the same release rather than a later one.

Planning mutations (milestone create/edit/archive/delete, decision create/edit/delete) returned {record, result}; result was the identical {kind:'success', revision} write receipt QCLI-264 unwrapped everywhere else, so they now return the record. Draft reads (draft view, draft list) returned the repository's {draft, location} pair -- the only reads in the CLI where the record was not the payload, since task view/list have carried path inline since QCLI-220 -- and now carry the draft's own fields with location inline.

Two decisions worth their reasons, since 'a decision exists' was the acceptance criterion:
1. location keeps its name rather than becoming path. It is what --include-archived callers distinguish on, its values are unchanged (drafts, archive/drafts), and a rename would be a second break for no gain. Pinned by a test asserting archive/drafts is still distinguishable after flattening.
2. The service layer is untouched: listDrafts still returns LocatedDraft and only the CLI's presentation flattens, so nothing internal (nextDraftId at src/cli/main.ts:549 reads record.draft.id off the service type) changes.

The invariant now holds everywhere: every read and every write, in all four groups, carries the record in data. The one deliberate exception is task edit-batch, a batch report rather than a record, which QCLI-264 already pinned with its reason stated.

Verified, not assumed: bun run check green (449 pass, 0 fail); PR #4 green on all ten checks and squash-merged to dev as 8085f26. test/qcli265-planning-and-read-shape.test.ts pins the planning shape, the draft read shape including the archived case, and -- the point of the file -- one test asserting the whole invariant across all four groups at once, so a command added later that picks a wrapper shape has something to fail. Nine existing assertions reading data.record/data.draft were updated rather than deleted.

Consumers enumerated by BARE FIELD NAME before the change (record, result, draft, location; 194 hits read across opum-cli-e2e, lore-cli and opum-fleet), with the matched pattern recorded so the next reader can see the blind spot's shape -- QCLI-264's idiom-shaped grep had missed a reversed-order fallback, which is why this sweep matched the field name alone. One break, opum-cli-e2e 45-parity-backlog.mjs:298, reported to its owner with the tolerant form its own line 448 already uses.

One stale claim removed on the way: QCLI-264's changelog paragraph said the planning group was out of scope and deferred to QCLI-265. True when written, false once 265 joined the same release, and it would have shipped in the release notes.
